en.title: Index Pairs Satisfying Both Absolute-Value Inequalities
en.description:
Count the index pairs with 0≤i<j<n that satisfy both min(|x−y|,|x+y|)≤min(|x|,|y|) and max(|x−y|,|x+y|)≥max(|x|,|y|), where x=a[i] and y=a[j]. Repeated values are counted separately by index.

The ranges added by this site for missing bounds and the recovery of source typos are described in the input protocol.
en.input: The input gives n and n integers. Full original bounds: 2≤n≤200000, −10^9≤a[i]≤10^9; the raw source restores the i<j condition that the catalog's HTML filtering swallowed.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 2; 1; 2. They have been checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Take absolute values and sort. With a≤b, the two inequalities become b−a≤a and b+a≥b, so only b≤2a is needed; count the index pairs in the window with two pointers.
